children: OTTAWA, Ontario and SAN FRANCISCO, Sept. 02, 2026
-- Telesat LEO ULC, a subsidiary of

(Nasdaq and TSX: TSAT), one of the world’s largest and most innovative satellite operators, and Farcast, a San Francisco-based startup building advanced satellite user terminals, today announced the successful completion of a collaborative technology demonstration program.

Building on their previously announced agreement, the two companies have successfully demonstrated key capabilities of Farcast's electronically steered antenna (ESA) technology through an extensive development and test program. The work validates Farcast's innovative architecture, which reduces hardware complexity without compromising performance and significantly lowers size, weight, power, and cost (SWaP-C).

The program culminated in an over-the-air demonstration using Telesat's LEO 3 test satellite. Farcast successfully established and maintained end-to-end satellite connectivity through its shared-aperture user terminal, with measured performance closely matching predicted link budgets. The results provide strong validation of the underlying terminal technology. This milestone paves the way for the next phase of the collaboration: the development of a fully integrated user terminal for the Telesat Lightspeed network, bringing together Farcast's antenna platform and the Telesat Lightspeed modem solution.

“The results mark an important step in validating Farcast's underlying antenna technology,” said Michel Forest, Chief Technology Officer for Telesat. “This work provides a strong foundation for the next phase of user terminal integration and development.”

“The progress we’ve made over the past four years is a testament to the incredible teamwork and close collaboration between Telesat and Farcast,” said Siamak Ebadi, founder and CEO of Farcast. “We’re very excited to build on this foundation as we move into modem integration and toward production for Telesat Lightspeed.”

About Telesat

Telesat Corporation (Nasdaq and TSX: TSAT) (“Telesat”) is a global satellite operator and leader in advanced satellite communications, redefining broadband connectivity through its Telesat Lightspeed Low Earth Orbit (LEO) network. Designed from inception for interoperability with enterprise and government applications, Telesat Lightspeed delivers secure, resilient, high-performance broadband connectivity with fibre-like speeds. Its advanced, software-defined architecture operates in both commercial and military Ka-band spectrum, enabling mission-critical communications with enhanced security and protection against evolving threats. Purpose-built to meet the most demanding requirements, Telesat Lightspeed provides telecom, enterprise, aviation, maritime and defence customers with unprecedented flexibility and control to dynamically manage their own services and deliver differentiated, end-to-end connectivity solutions worldwide.

With nearly 60 years of innovation, engineering excellence and a collaborative approach to customer success, Telesat is uniquely positioned to deliver secure, scalable and future-ready connectivity solutions that help customers solve their most complex communications challenges and achieve mission success. For updates on Telesat, follow us on LinkedIn, X, or visit www.telesat.com.
About Farcast

Founded in 2019 and headquartered in San Francisco, California, Farcast develops next-generation electronically steered satellite user terminals designed to significantly reduce size, weight, power, and cost (SWaP-C) while delivering high-performance broadband connectivity. The company’s proprietary phased-array technology simplifies terminal architecture for commercial, enterprise, mobility, government, and defence applications.

Since its founding, Farcast has partnered with industry leaders including Telesat, Viasat, Anuvu, and the U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) on technology development programs that have matured and demonstrated its core platform. The company is backed by strategic investors including Telesat, Gogo, and Lockheed Martin and is now focused on transitioning its technology into commercial production for next-generation satellite networks.
